frame_28.jpg.note: Tiny, stiff, near-identical blocky figures stand in rigid rows like game pieces. They sit on a flat sandy plane with no contact shadows or scale cues. The cannonball piles and crates are simple primitives.

frame_68.jpg.note: The figures have box torsos, stick legs, flat tricorn hats and slab feet. The marching poses are stiff and repeated across the crowd. The lighting is decent, with raking sun and a long shadow. Even so, the figures look like low-poly wooden pieces, and the cloned crowd is obvious.

frame_62.jpg.note: The same blocky low-poly figures as frame_68, with a slightly different pose set. The legs are stiff scissor strides. Faces and hands are crude, and the clothing is flat shapes with no cloth detail. The clone-army crowd reads as a diorama, though the sunlit ground is passable.

frame_46.jpg.note: Tiny blocky figures are scattered on the rampart, some in loose poses, with a few red-coated figures carrying boxes. They have no weight, no foot contact and no real scale relation to the cannons and stone. The result is a wargame-miniature look against a decent wall texture.
